subject: Regional data exit & erasure procedures - hosted API Q&A
messages:
From: Sasha Coleman <sasha@larkpay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: LarkPay Security <security@larkpay.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - residency/retention/erasures (quick Qs)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing a questionnaire for our legal/security review and need short, definitive answers for the hosted API:

1) Where does customer data (requests + model responses) physically live by default? Any regional pinning options?
2) What's the timeline for a customer-initiated erasure request (hot storage vs backups)?
3) Do you retain model logs, prompts, or embeddings for training? If so, can we opt out?
4) What controls/documentation can you provide to prove deletion (audit logs, attestations)?

Our procurement team is on a tight deadline next week — any concise answers and a pointer to artifacts would help.

Appreciate it,
Sasha
Security & Ops
LarkPay

[Attachment: larkpay-questionnaire.pdf (PDF)]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Coleman <sasha@larkpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, LarkPay Security <security@larkpay.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API - residency/retention/erasures (quick Qs)

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can drop into the questionnaire; I included conservative SLAs and the artifacts we can attach. Happy to hop on a call if you want a walk-through.

1) Default residency and regional pinning
- Default: customer request/response payloads for Redwood Hosted live in the AWS region selected at account creation (we currently support us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1).
- Regional pinning: available as a tenant-level option for hosted customers (documented in the Console). Add-on for guaranteed region-lock is available for enterprise plans and requires a short provisioning window.

2) Erasure timeline (customer-initiated)
- Hot data (primary stores and caches): removal initiated within 24 hours and typically completed within 72 hours.
- Background KV/prefix caches: ephemeral by design; caching windows are workload-dependent and typically expire within 24 hours. We purge any cached context related to the tenant as part of erasure.
- Backups/snapshots: rolling backups are retained for disaster-recovery and are overwritten or deleted according to the backup retention period. Full deletion from immutable backup chains completes within 90 days from the erasure request in our standard hosted offering.
- Verification: once erasure completes we will provide a deletion ticket ID and an audit entry (see #4).

3) Use of data for training and opt-out
- Redwood does not use customer prompt/response data to train our base models by default.
- We may analyze aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement (latency/error metrics) — these metrics do not include PII or full prompt text.
- Opt-out: customers can request no-data-retention at the tenant level (turns off request logging for non-billing/troubleshooting use cases). Note: opting out may limit some debugging features and product analytics.

4) Controls and proof of deletion
- Audit logs: every erasure request generates an immutable audit entry (ticket ID, requester, timestamp, affected tenant id). We can export the audit trail for a given request window as a CSV/JSON.
- Attestations: we can provide a deletion confirmation letter signed by Redwood (standard format) and include the ticket ID.
- Evidence pack: for enterprise/procurement we provide a one-off evidence package (incl. operation logs, S3 object deletion markers, and snapshot retention metadata).

Security controls (short bullets)
- Data encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit. Hosted keys are stored in an HSM-managed keystore.
- Access: role-based access controls (RBAC), least privilege, and human access requires an approved ticket.
- SOC2: we are SOC 2 type II audited (control reports available under NDA).

Artifacts we can attach: DPA Exhibit A (data handling), redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf, deletion-attestation-template.docx. I attached the flow diagram; will upload the DPA exhibit on request.

If you want stricter guarantees (regional-only data + shorter backup wipe windows) we can discuss a dedicated or private deployment option — that requires procurement.

Best,
Irene
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf (PDF)]

One small add on timelines:
- Emergency deletion (for legal/compliance escalations) — we can accelerate hot-store purges to within 4–8 hours once the request is validated and the ticket is approved by our Escalations team.
- Audit exports: typical turnaround for an evidence pack is 3 business days for hosted customers; 1 business day for enterprise customers with an SLA.

- We'll want the deletion confirmation letter + ticket ID attached to our contract exhibit; can you send the template for internal review?

If easier I can open a support ticket and we can move the evidence pack request there.

Best,
Sasha
